policy_title: Introduce Capital Gains Tax Relief for Landlords Selling to Tenants
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce a two-year temporary Capital Gains Tax relief for landlords who sell their properties to their existing tenants.

source.quote: To further support homeowners, we will introduce a two-year temporary Capital Gains Tax relief for landlords who sell to their existing tenants.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly incentivises landlords to sell to sitting tenants via a CGT discount, affecting tenure security, homeownership access for lower-income renters, and private rental stock — all core O1 indicators.
CGT relief directly reduces the tax payable by landlords on qualifying disposals, improving their post-tax proceeds — a clear, first-order change to a household tax burden.

Forgone CGT revenue on qualifying sales is a concrete fiscal cost; the two-year window limits scale but HMRC receipts from residential CGT are non-trivial, and the relief is unconditional on other fiscal offsets.

Tax benefit accrues primarily to landlords (a higher-wealth demographic) while simultaneously enabling tenant wealth-accumulation via homeownership — the distributional direction is genuinely contested, warranting a real verdict on the gap.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear: the policy is simultaneously a housing-tenure intervention (O1), a landlord tax break (O11), a revenue-cost measure (O12), and a distributional policy with rival wealth effects (O14). Effects on O5, O3, O7 etc. are negligible or purely incidental.
